title: fix(sse): stabilize streaming framing + partial-JSON delimiter ordering
author: Jordan Li
description:
Motivation: customers reported intermittent invalid partial-JSON payloads and out-of-order SSE / token events when using the OpenAI-compat streaming path. Root causes: (1) delimiter handling in the SSE aggregator could split JSON token boundaries when a token payload contained the streaming delimiter sequence; (2) the streamer could flush an event before downstream framing finished assembling a partial JSON object (race on the framing buffer); (3) the compatibility layer applied an extra '
' normalization pass that changed event ordering in edge cases. This PR addresses all three by: 1) making the parser delimiter-aware (delimiters matched only at event boundaries, not inside quoted JSON strings), 2) introducing an assembly queue that guarantees partial-JSON fragments are re-ordered and re-joined before emission, and 3) removing the normalization pass from the OpenAI compatibility shim and handling canonicalization in a single place. Changes include a new deterministic reassembly algorithm, tests that exercise delimiter-in-string cases and multi-chunk JSON objects, and minor perf optimizations to keep latency impact under 1ms/payload on our benchmarks. Checklist: - [x] add unit tests for delimiter-in-string and multi-chunk object assembly - [x] add integration test against openai-compat harness - [x] benchmark to measure added latency - [x] include docs note in specs/sse.md - [x] add changelog/release note. Related: Linear ENG-9483 (streaming stability), ENG-9521 (openai compat edge cases).
